findings.title: Debug tracing left in at Error level, dumping full ID lists
findings.description:
Six `r.log.Error(...)` calls (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) fire on every batch of the normal success path.
- **Not errors:** the "to clean" calls sit after the `if err != nil { return }` check, so their `"err", err` field is always nil.
- **Volume:** each logs the whole `ids` slice (up to `cleanupjob_batchsize` entries; the new test uses 32767) plus the raw SQL condition.
- **Always on:** `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` runs its batch at least once per call, so it emits two error lines even when there is nothing to delete.

This will flood error logs and trip error-rate alerting. Remove the calls, or downgrade to `Debug` with counts only.

findings.title: Global cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.description:
`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)` looks like a testing leftover and is unrelated to the deadlock fix.
- **Scope:** it makes every job in `clean()` run ten times as often — snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, query history, not just annotations.
- **Broken invariant:** `clean()` keeps `const timeout = 9 * time.Minute` at line 89, sized to fit inside the old 10-minute interval. A run can now span up to nine ticks.
- **Compounding:** it multiplies the error-log spam above and the Info-level "Completed cleanup jobs" line by ten.

Revert to `time.Minute * 10`.

findings.title: Quadratic string building for the SQLite inlined-ID path
findings.description: `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` recopies the whole accumulated string on every iteration. For the 32767-ID batch the new test targets, that is gigabytes of cumulative copying to build a ~230 KB statement. Use a `strings.Builder` with `strconv.AppendInt`.

findings.title: Parameter-count limits only handled for SQLite; batch size is unbounded
findings.description:
The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID. `cleanupjob_batchsize` is read with `MustInt64(100)` and no upper bound (`pkg/setting/setting.go:710`).
- **Postgres/MySQL:** both cap bind parameters at 65535 per statement, so a larger batch size worked with the old single statement and will now fail every run.
- **SQLite:** a very large batch can exceed the default 1 MB statement-length limit on the inlined path.

Either chunk `ids` inside `deleteByIDs` or clamp the setting at load time.

findings.title: Placeholder names and misleading helper contract in new code
findings.description:
- **Naming:** `x, y := r.deleteByIDs(...)` appears three times (lines 536, 556, 578) and exists only to feed the debug logs. It should be `return r.deleteByIDs(ctx, table, ids)`.
- **Parameter name:** `fetchIDs`'s `condition` actually carries `WHERE` predicates plus `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`; the name hides that.
- **Guard order:** the empty-condition check at lines 586-588 runs after the SQL string has started being built; it belongs first.
- **Stale comment:** "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" (line 605) is only true before SQLite 3.32, while the test name refers to the 3.32+ limit.

findings.title: Three near-identical fetch/log/delete closures
findings.description: The MaxAge, MaxCount and orphaned-tag closures differ only in table name and condition string. A single helper such as `r.cleanBatch(ctx, table, cond)` would remove the triplication, and with it the six copies of the logging calls.

findings.title: Test gaps: multi-ID placeholder path untested on SQLite; cleanup registered late
findings.description:
- **Coverage hole:** cases use batch size 1 (one placeholder) or 32767 (inlined path on SQLite). The `"?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)` branch with more than one ID is never exercised on SQLite, the default CI database, even though the production default is 100. Add a case with a batch size between 2 and 999.
- **Late cleanup:** `t.Cleanup` is registered after `createTestAnnotations` and two `require`-based assertions. If any of those fail, rows stay in the shared `fakeSQL` and cascade into later subtests, made worse by the now-fixed explicit IDs. Register the cleanup first.
- **Inconsistent cleanup:** `TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst` (lines 158-164) still deletes only `annotation`, not `annotation_tag`.
- **Stale case name:** "running the max count delete again…" no longer runs anything again; each subtest now seeds its own data.

findings.title: Explicit primary keys in test fixtures
findings.description: `ID: int64(i + 1)` is needed so tag rows can reference annotations in a bulk insert. On Postgres, explicit IDs do not advance the sequence, so a later auto-increment insert into the same database could collide if rows survive. It is safe today only because each subtest deletes everything.

findings.title: Batching loop refactor preserves semantics
findings.description: `untilDoneOrCancelled` keeps the previous termination conditions (context cancelled, error, zero rows affected) and accumulates `totalAffected` correctly. The MaxCount branch now falls through to the shared return with no behaviour change. `min` and `errors.Join` are available under the module's `go 1.21`.
